To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) honorific use by Japanese speakers is a matter of the speaker’s choice of a specific honorific expression in a specific situation, (2) this choice is influenced by the social identity of addressee and referent, and (3) this choice is also influenced by the social identities of other people in the speech situation.

Japanese honorific use is an indexical of the speaker’s situational stance, and that this indexicality is not a matter of rule-governed behavior but of the speaker’s strategic selection from a range of options.
